goal:
T35 — the service decides its own harness adoption (roadmap M2: champion vs challenger).

Since release 5 every eval accepts harness_version ("api-sealed-eval/1" strict hunk counts, "api-sealed-eval/2" recount)
and records it on the measurement; performance.compare implements the rule (improved only when the challenger's Wilson
lower bound is above the champion's upper bound).

1. services/api/main.py: POST /v1/eval/abtest {suite_version (v0|v1|v2, default v2), kind (X_SINGLE|PIPELINE),
   family (optional), model (default muse-spark-1.3), champion, challenger} where champion/challenger are harness
   versions (same Literal as the eval requests). Same harness for both -> 400. Budget guard for BOTH runs before any
   provider call (402). Runs as ONE background eval job (reuse services/api/evoforge/eval_jobs.py: one job at a time,
   202 + GET /v1/eval/jobs/{id}); the worker runs the champion measurement then the challenger measurement through the
   same helpers as the sync endpoints (_do_eval_baseline/_do_eval_pipeline with the harness argument), so both are
   recorded like any other measurement.
2. The job result has "decision": {decision_id, created_at, suite_version, kind, model, family, champion, challenger,
   champion_measurement, challenger_measurement, verdict (improved|no_clear_difference|worse from the same Wilson rule),
   decision: "adopt" only when verdict == improved else "keep", reason (e.g. "improved: lo 0.61 > hi 0.39" or
   "no_clear_difference: intervals overlap")}.
3. Store decisions (NEW services/api/evoforge/decisions.py, in-process list like eval_jobs, thread-safe) and expose
   GET /v1/eval/decisions -> {"decisions": [...]} newest first, at most 50. (Persistence can follow later.)
4. apps/web/lib/proxyPolicy.ts + proxyPolicy.cases.json: allow POST /v1/eval/abtest and GET /v1/eval/decisions.
5. Tests: services/api/tests/test_muse_t35.py. Do not change sealed_eval.py or patch.py.
